title: TOPA Propaganda & Information Influence Defensive Manual v0.1
mission: Understand how propaganda and influence operations function well enough to recognize, investigate, falsify and counter them while preserving evidence, rights and uncertainty.
non_goal: This manual is not a guide for designing persuasion campaigns, microtargeting populations, covert influence, deception, or psychological operations against real audiences.

core_model.formula: ACTOR/INCENTIVE -> NARRATIVE -> CONTENT/CLAIM -> CHANNEL/AMPLIFICATION -> AUDIENCE EXPOSURE -> COGNITIVE/SOCIAL MECHANISM -> BEHAVIOR/ATTITUDE EFFECT -> FEEDBACK/ADAPTATION

analysis_layers.name: ARTIFACT
analysis_layers.question: What exact claim, image, video, phrase, statistic or omission exists?

analysis_layers.name: PROVENANCE
analysis_layers.question: Who first published it, when, where, through which account/domain/document, and can the chain be reproduced?

analysis_layers.name: CONTENT_TECHNIQUE
analysis_layers.question: Which observable rhetorical or evidentiary techniques appear without inferring intent from style alone?

analysis_layers.name: DISTRIBUTION_BEHAVIOR
analysis_layers.question: Is amplification organic, coordinated, paid, automated, cross-platform, recycled or source-root duplicated?

analysis_layers.name: NARRATIVE_GRAPH
analysis_layers.question: Which repeated frames/claims are related, and which are merely semantically similar?

analysis_layers.name: AUDIENCE_EFFECT
analysis_layers.question: Is there evidence of actual belief/behavior change rather than reach, views or engagement?

analysis_layers.name: ATTRIBUTION
analysis_layers.question: What evidence links the activity to an actor? Infrastructure, timing, assets, documents, admissions, platform takedowns or independent investigations?

analysis_layers.name: COUNTERMEASURE
analysis_layers.question: Which response has evidence, what are side effects, and what would falsify claimed effectiveness?

common_observable_mechanisms.name: REPETITION_AND_FAMILIARITY
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Repeated exposure can increase familiarity and perceived truth; log first-seen time and source-root count rather than raw repetition count.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: HIGH_VOLUME_MULTI_CHANNEL
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Volume can overwhelm verification capacity; collapse duplicated source roots and prioritize claims by harm, reach and evidence.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: CARD_STACKING_OR_SELECTIVE_EVIDENCE
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Check omitted base rates, denominators, time windows, comparison classes and contrary evidence.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: EMOTIONAL_AROUSAL
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Fear, anger, disgust, pride or urgency can reduce reflective checking; separate emotional cue from factual proposition.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: FALSE_AUTHORITY_OR_TESTIMONIAL
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Verify identity, expertise, quote context and whether authority actually supports the specific claim.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: BANDWAGON_OR_SOCIAL_PROOF
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Engagement metrics and apparent consensus are not independent evidence; check coordinated amplification and inauthentic patterns.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: SCAPEGOATING_AND_OUTGROUP_FRAMING
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Decompose group-level claims into specific falsifiable propositions and watch for dehumanization or identity-based manipulation.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: FALSE_DILEMMA_AND_FORCED_BINARY
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Enumerate plausible third options and mixed explanations before accepting a binary frame.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: CONSPIRATORIAL_SELF_SEALING
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Ask what evidence could disconfirm the claim; if every contrary observation is reinterpreted as proof, flag CLOSED_BELIEF_LOOP.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: IMPOSTOR_OR_FORGED_SOURCE
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Check original domain/account, archive snapshots, document metadata, visual provenance and official source confirmation.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: CONTEXT_STRIPPING
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Recover surrounding video/text, date, place, original language and prior publication history.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: LAUNDERING_THROUGH_INTERMEDIARIES
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Trace citations backward until the earliest accessible root; many outlets may still be one source.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: COORDINATED_INAUTHENTIC_AMPLIFICATION
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Look for synchronized timing, repeated assets, shared infrastructure, identical phrasing and account-network anomalies; coordination is not inferred from agreement alone.

common_observable_mechanisms.name: AI_GENERATED_OR_SYNTHETIC_MEDIA
common_observable_mechanisms.defensive_read: Use provenance, reverse search, metadata, source continuity and independent event records; detector scores alone are weak evidence.

actions: map observable tactics using FIMI/DISARM-like taxonomy
separate content truth from manipulation behavior
teach general manipulation technique before exposure where evidence supports it
use weakened examples rather than live persuasion optimization
state false claim only as needed
explain why it is wrong and provide an alternative causal account
share indicators and TTPs with defenders
legal/policy response only under rights and proportionality constraints

countermeasure_evidence_notes: Debunking and fact-checking often reduce misperceptions, but effects vary by context and do not guarantee behavioral change.
Prebunking/inoculation has evidence for improving recognition of manipulation techniques, but protection can wane and should be evaluated.
Accuracy prompts show replicable average effects on sharing discernment in experimental work, but platform/context generalization should be tested.
No single intervention should be assumed sufficient; combined approaches and whole-of-society resilience may be more robust.
Countermeasures can backfire through amplification, censorship perceptions, reactance or loss of trust; these are explicit falsifiers and side effects.

red_team_firewall.allowed: Use red-team taxonomies to recognize observable tactics and generate defensive tests.
not_allowed: optimize emotional triggers for a real target group
select vulnerable demographic audiences for influence
design covert personas or fake grassroots campaigns
advise on evasion of platform moderation or attribution

janus_spiral: ARTIFACT_0 -> PROVENANCE -> TACTIC -> DISTRIBUTION -> EFFECT_EVIDENCE -> COUNTERMEASURE -> REVERSE_NECESSITY -> ARTIFACT_PRIME_1
reverse_questions: If the claimed influence effect were real, what observable audience evidence must exist upstream?
If attribution were correct, what infrastructure/provenance evidence must pre-exist?
If a countermeasure worked, what baseline/control or behavioral signal must change?
Which forward node is merely assumed because the story is coherent?
What alternative non-propaganda explanation fits the same artifact/distribution pattern?
